classification.difficultyReason: Two right triangles share an intermediate pole height; the second sine ratio must be rearranged.

content.prompt: A flagpole is stabilised by two cables affixed to the top of the pole. One of these makes a $38^{\circ}$ angle to the ground and is 5.5 metres long. The second cable makes an angle of $48^{\circ}$ to the ground. How long is the second cable? Give your answer to two decimal places.

spec.description: Two cables meet at the top of a vertical pole and terminate at ground anchors on opposite sides. The decorative pink flag is omitted. Ordinary geometry is black and unshaded.
spec.mathematics: The left cable has length 5.5 and ground angle 38 degrees. The right cable has length x and ground angle 48 degrees. Both triangles share perpendicular pole height y; the pole base has a right-angle marker.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels are visible; no calculated lengths are supplied.

answer.short:
$4.56\text{ m}$

Find the shared pole height using the first cable, then use the sine ratio for the second cable.
